summary.summary: Powys's Q4 report to 31 March 2026 shows total borrowing down £5.61m over the year to £362.03m even after £25m of new PWLB in Q4, with the CFR closing at £453.34m — £22.7m below the original estimate because capital schemes were reprofiled and extra Welsh Government grants landed. Financing costs came in at 3.8% of net revenue against 4.0% planned, but the report is explicit that the deferred borrowing 'will still be required in the future': the CFR is forecast to reach £614.20m by March 2028. The council was an active short-term lender to other authorities (£35.32m across six loans in Q4, all repaid by March 2026). Aged sundry debt rose £3.0m in the quarter to £15.51m, 73% of the over-three-month debt being hard-to-collect social care charges; all treasury prudential indicators were complied with.

signals.headline: Total borrowing fell £5.61m in 2025/26 to £362.03m at 31 March 2026 despite £25m of new PWLB in Q4; financing costs 3.8% of net revenue (£13.94m) vs 4.0% in the approved strategy
signals.why: A year of modest deleveraging with capital financing costs inside plan, helped by reprofiling and additional Welsh Government grants.

signals.headline: CFR forecast to rise from £453.34m at 31 March 2026 to £516.13m by March 2027 and £614.20m by March 2028 (+£161m in two years); the report states deferred borrowing 'will still be required in the future'
signals.why: This year's saving is a deferral, not an avoidance — the capital programme implies substantial new external borrowing at forecast PWLB rates above 5%.

news_drafts.headline: Growing Mid Wales Board faces delivery risks across £110m investment portfolio
news_drafts.lead: Six of seven major projects in Powys's £110 million Growing Mid Wales capital investment programme have been rated Amber on delivery confidence by formal gateway reviews, indicating material risks that require active management. The board's governance statement identifies financial profiling and funding drawdown — the pace and timing of capital deployment — as principal risks to the portfolio. A small number of projects required intervention to review delivery assumptions and refine financial profiles. The governance framework for the £110 million programme is undergoing its first full year of formal financial reporting, with Audit Wales scheduled to undertake external audit engagement in early 2027 following threshold changes and the move to full Statement of Accounts.

news_drafts.headline: Powys cleared by auditor as council flags financial sustainability risk
news_drafts.lead: The Auditor General has issued an unqualified opinion on Powys County Council's 2025/26 accounts, confirming the financial statements are reliable and free of material misstatement. The clearance comes as the council's risk register identifies financial sustainability over the short and medium term as its core strategic concern, with a residual risk score of 16 out of 25. The council has strengthened its reserves and updated its medium-term financial planning in the first quarter, but faces ongoing uncertainty around future funding settlements, inflationary pressures, pay awards and demand-led service costs. Separately, the council has flagged school premises maintenance as under-funded and is preparing a business case to secure additional funding, while adult social care waiting times have fallen but nursing bed capacity and care package costs remain problematic. Audit Wales found the council has a good understanding of its workforce recruitment challenges and is successfully using a range of approaches to address them.
news_drafts.paper_title: 20.10.26 Qtr 1 2026-2027 App A NON-CONFIDENTIAL strategic risks

news_drafts.headline: Powys Council internal audit findings deteriorate as governance weakens
news_drafts.lead: Powys Council's internal audit findings deteriorated significantly in 2025-26. Only 2.7% of audited areas achieved substantial assurance that controls were working well, compared with 7.69% the previous year, while limited assurance findings (indicating control weaknesses) rose to 27% of areas examined. The council's governance statement recorded downgrade of three principles, including financial management and internal control, from substantial to reasonable assurance. The council achieved a balanced budget for 2026-27 and received an unqualified opinion on its 2024-25 accounts with no misstatements. However, it can only demonstrate financial balance one year ahead, and a new financial system was embedded in April 2026 during this period of declining governance assurance.

findings.committee: Bwrdd Tyfu Canolbarth Cymru / Growing Mid Wales Board
findings.headline: Governance framework and accountable body controls are subject to formal review, with first full Statement of Accounts in preparation.
findings.detail: The action plan includes commissioning internal audit review of the governance framework following the first year of full Statement of Accounts preparation, and Audit Wales will undertake external audit engagement following threshold changes and the move to full Statement of Accounts. This indicates the governance and financial accounting framework for the £110m portfolio has recently moved to a higher level of formality and is still embedding.
findings.matters: Accountable body controls and formal external audit are essential safeguards for £110m of public investment; the fact that these are being formally established (rather than operating under established arrangements) suggests the control environment is relatively recent and may not yet be fully tested.
findings.figures: Internal Audit Review scheduled Q3 2026–27; Audit Wales engagement Q1 & Q2 2026–27; Accountable Body controls review 2026–27.
findings.quote: To commission an annual Internal Audit Review of the Governance Framework following the 1st year of full Statement of Accounts preparation... Prepare for Audit Wales external audit engagement following threshold changes and the move to full Statement of Accounts.

findings.committee: Bwrdd Tyfu Canolbarth Cymru / Growing Mid Wales Board
findings.headline: A small number of projects required intervention, including review of delivery assumptions and refinement of financial profiles.
findings.detail: The statement notes that some projects needed closer oversight and intervention, with specific mention of reviewing delivery assumptions and refining financial profiles. This indicates that initial project plans underestimated risks or misaligned resources, requiring mid-course correction.
findings.matters: Corrective actions on delivery assumptions suggest earlier business cases may have been optimistic; refinement of financial profiles indicates reprofiling of spend and timeline, which affects when benefits will be realised and cash demands on partner authorities.
findings.figures: Number of cases requiring intervention not specified; scale and nature of financial profile refinements not disclosed.
findings.quote: In a small number of cases, risks required closer oversight or intervention, including review of delivery assumptions, refinement of financial profiles and strengthening of project controls.

findings.committee: Bwrdd Tyfu Canolbarth Cymru / Growing Mid Wales Board
findings.headline: Financial profiling and funding drawdown identified as principal portfolio risk.
findings.detail: The governance statement explicitly identifies financial profiling and the ability to draw down funding as principal risks. This suggests uncertainty about the pace and timing of capital deployment across the £110m programme, which affects cash flow and timeline to generating the economic returns the investment is intended to create.
findings.matters: For a lender, uncertain drawdown profiles create refinancing risk and affect the council's cash position; for a finance director, they signal either overambitious project timelines or delivery obstacles that may delay benefits realisation.
findings.figures: £110 million capital investment commitment (excluding local authority, private sector and other match funding).
findings.quote: During 2025–2026, the principal risks and issues identified across the portfolio related to delivery confidence and project readiness, financial profiling and funding drawdown, and the management of dependencies across programmes and external delivery partners.

findings.committee: Bwrdd Tyfu Canolbarth Cymru / Growing Mid Wales Board
findings.headline: Most gateway reviews rated Amber on delivery confidence rather than Green.
findings.detail: Between July 2025 and February 2026, seven formal gateway or project assessment reviews were completed covering major Growth Deal programmes. Of these, six were rated Amber and one was Green/Amber. Amber indicates material risks to successful delivery that require active management.
findings.matters: Delivery confidence ratings indicate whether the £110m portfolio is on track to deploy funds and achieve outcomes on schedule; Amber across most major projects suggests execution risks.
findings.figures: Seven gateway reviews: Elan Valley Lakes (Amber), Strategic Portfolio Business Case (Green/Amber), Montgomery Canal (Amber), Agri-Food Business Park (Amber), MWCPIF (Amber), GFIP OBC (Amber), Mid Wales Broadband (Amber/Green).
findings.quote: During 2025–2026, the principal risks and issues identified across the portfolio related to delivery confidence and project readiness, financial profiling and funding drawdown, and the management of dependencies across programmes and external delivery partners.

findings.paper_title: PCC SWAP Internal Audit Activity Report Sept 2026
findings.headline: Strong fraud and error detection recovered £27,695 in NFI overpayments, identified £60,000+ in council tax errors, and 2 confirmed frauds
findings.detail: The National Fraud Initiative work identified £27,695 in overpayments, 2 confirmed frauds, and £48,165 in estimated fraud prevention savings. Separately, the Council Tax Single Person Discount exercise identified errors valued at over £60,000 with potential savings exceeding £121,000. Earlier expenses audits also identified £22,822 in overpayments for recovery.
findings.matters: Demonstrates an effective control environment able to identify and recover lost money; the scale of recoveries (£148,000+ across programs) indicates systematic review catching errors that would otherwise remain undetected
findings.figures: £27,695 NFI overpayments recovered, 2 confirmed frauds, £48,165 estimated fraud prevention savings, £60,000+ council tax errors identified, £121,000+ potential savings, £22,822 expenses recovered
findings.quote: Investigations have also delivered tangible outcomes, identifying £27,695 in overpayments, 44 data errors, 2 confirmed frauds, and an estimated £48,165 in fraud prevention savings. In addition, the Council Tax Single Person Discount exercise has identified errors valued at over £60,000 and potential savings exceeding £121,000
